answer.rationale: The competitive pressure from aggressive entry pricing requires immediate defense of the SMB segment where we have documented strength. Memory_73 shows promotional pricing is proven effective for price-sensitive SMB acquisition and revenue lift. Memory_31 demonstrates signup simplification works for the same segment. The 6% activation decline and 4% onboarding drop suggest our core funnel is losing efficiency—likely to competitive switching. A targeted promotional pricing experiment (standard scope) addresses the acute threat while preserving our long-term revenue quality by following the established playbook. We verify memory_73 and memory_31 to confirm methodology and baseline lift before deploying. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well but require existing customer goodwill, which is at risk if we lose SMB segments to competitors first. Activation messaging (memory_91) and enterprise sales assist (memory_44) are valuable but don't directly counter the pricing pressure driving churn. Simplified onboarding (memory_86) complements but doesn't solve the conversion leakage at entry. One week capacity demands focus on the highest-leverage lever: stopping SMB attrition through proven promotional mechanics.
